thread:
liam: Heads-up — sirocco-6.7b-q rolled to prod on Dedicated r3 this morning. Seeing weird date hallucinations (2024 → 1976) and token repeat when prompts include numeric sequences. Throughput also dropped ~15% vs baseline. Anyone else?

anya: saw alerts from the eval pipeline — DETOK N-gram entropy down, date-parser tests failing. Put an example below. :eyes:

anya: Example input -> model output:
```
PROMPT: 
User: "My flight is on 2024-11-02, confirm date?"
MODEL: "Your flight is scheduled for November 2, 1976. Please confirm."
```

devon: can you paste perf numbers and the exact quant config?

liam: perf snapshot (just after rollout):
```
model: sirocco-6.7b-q (q6-nf4-perchannel)
host: ded-r3-03
p50: 68ms (baseline 58ms)
p95: 420ms (baseline 360ms)
qps: 850 (baseline 1000)
KV-cache hit-rate: 78% (baseline 90%)
```

bench-bot: auto-run summary: quant profile q6-nf4-perchannel applied; kernel fallback observed on fused_attention for ~17% of requests; input token length distribution skewed by numeric-heavy prompts; KV cache miss rate increased ~12%.

karla: this reads like a quantization + kernel fallback interaction or tokeniser mismatch. Which sentencepiece/split config did the onboarding use?

liam: qconfig: `q6-nf4-perchannel-local` (we picked per-channel because it fixed a liberty-phrasing regression before). Tokeniser shipped with the onboarding binary: sentencepiece v0.1.99, with custom normalizer. Catalog still has v0.1.95.

devon: repro steps I recommend: 1) curl the dedicated canary with the exact header we use in prod 2) force deterministic sampling (temp=0.0) 3) run with 3 different seeds and compare token ids. Example: 
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://dedicated.redwood/sirocco-6.7b-q/call \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"prompt":"My flight is on 2024-11-02, confirm date?","max_tokens":60,"temperature":0.0}'
```

liam: opened ML-9234 for the quality regression and attached the failing eval shards + perf logs. Reverting canary?

sre_tony: please hold rollout and demote to 10% until we have a fix. @oncall can you rollback to previous quant snapshot if we keep seeing p95 > 400ms?

ops-bot: Deploy action logged: rollback-sirocco-1969123456 initiated by liam — canary traffic reduced to 5%.

anya: quick hypothesis — tokeniser version diff may change token IDs for numeric tokens, producing shifted embeddings that interact badly with per-channel scales. Can someone run a token-id diff for the string "2024-11-02" across v0.1.95 and v0.1.99?

liam: token id diff command I used: 
```python
from sentencepiece import SentencePieceProcessor
sp_old = SentencePieceProcessor(model_file='sp_v0.1.95.model')
sp_new = SentencePieceProcessor(model_file='sp_v0.1.99.model')
text = '2024-11-02'
print(sp_old.encode(text))
print(sp_new.encode(text))
```
Outputs: sp_v0.1.95 -> [48, 234, 9] ; sp_v0.1.99 -> [72, 234, 9] (example). Not huge but changes embedding index alignment.

karla: I'll run a quick quant sweep: per-tensor vs per-channel, and try smoothed calibration with the dates/urls set (50 samples). If per-tensor restores parity, we add that as a temporary profile and re-run QA.

devon: action items (short):
- hold rollout (done)
- reproducible local job (devon)
- tokeniser parity check + fix pipeline to use canonical model (anya)
- quant sweep + small eval (karla)
- add a regression test to CI for date parsing and numeric sequences (devon/anya)
- monitor KV-cache metrics and fused_attention fallbacks (tony)

liam: owners set: devon (repro & test), karla (quant sweep), anya (tokeniser parity), tony (rollback/observability). I also increased logging for cache hits for the next 2h.

liam: cc @infra if we need extra GPUs or a node with older sentencepiece lib for a proper A/B. Thanks all — keep updates here. :coffee:
